messages:
zoe li: Hey team! First week here — trying to get the local stack up on an M1 Mac. Running `docker compose up` and postgres keeps exiting during init with permission errors on the mounted ./pgdata dir. Anyone seen this?

zoe li: Logs: 
```
postgres_1  | initdb: could not create directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata": Permission denied
postgres_1  | initdb: removing contents of data directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata"
```

dan (eng): welcome! :wave: yep, mac bind mounts and postgres user ownership cause that. Two quick fixes: 1) use a docker named volume instead of bind-mounting a host folder, or 2) run an init step in the container as root to chown the dir. We prefer named volumes for dev.

charlie infra: also check image arch on M1 — if an amd64 layer is used via emulation, sometimes filesystem semantics differ. Run `docker inspect <container>` and check the "Architecture"/"Platform" fields.

zoe li: I switched to `volumes:
  - dev_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` and created the volume but now the app can't connect: connection refused. Postgres logs show it's listening on a socket only.

dan (eng): ensure `ports: - "5432:5432"` is present and PG listen_addresses allows TCP. In our compose we set `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `POSTGRES_DB`, and `PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata`. Also for M1 add `platform: linux/arm64` to the postgres service if the image doesn't multi-arch.

setup-bot: Dev docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/dev-setup#local-postgres (internal)

charlie infra: snippet we use in repo: 
```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:15
    platform: linux/arm64
    volumes:
      - dev_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: redwood
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: localpass
      POSTGRES_DB: redwood_dev
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
volumes:
  dev_pgdata:
    driver: local
```

zoe li: adding platform fixed the arch issue and postgres is up. One annoyance: host psql can't access DB because files are inside the volume and permissions are root-owned. Our `scripts/db-reset` expects to run `dropdb` locally. Any recommendations so scripts don't fail?

dan (eng): good question. We avoid host file ops on the DB volume. For CLI tasks, run commands in the container: `docker compose exec postgres psql -U redwood -d redwood_dev -c "SELECT 1;"` or have the helper script run a transient psql container that shares the same network/credentials. I can add a wrapper `scripts/psql-in-container` to the repo.

zoe li: that works for me. Thanks for the quick help! I'll update my onboarding notes.

charlie infra: optional: if you prefer a local native Postgres via Homebrew for very fast iteration, that's fine — set DATABASE_URL in `.env.local` and skip the container. But for parity with CI we recommend containers.

zoe li: resolved for my setup, thanks everyone :tada:
